crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Rolling Forecasts
children.blurb: Rolling forecasts are a planning method where the forecast horizon stays fixed while the calendar moves forward.

children.name: External Signals in Revenue Models
children.blurb: External signals in revenue models are the inputs from outside a company's own sales and billing systems that shape forecasts of future revenue.

children.name: Variance Analysis and Explanation
children.blurb: Variance analysis and explanation covers the comparison of actual financial and operational results against budgets, forecasts, prior periods, and driver-based plans.

children.name: Capital Spending Decisions
children.blurb: Capital spending decisions in an AI context cover the choices a company makes about long term investments in computing hardware, data platforms, software licenses, and the people needed to run them.

children.name: Zero-Based Budgeting
children.blurb: Zero-based budgeting is a planning method in which every cost line starts at zero for each new budget cycle and must be justified by a stated purpose, a cost driver, and an expected outcome.

sections.body: Forecasting and planning in accounting is the work of projecting revenue, costs, cash, and capital needs, then comparing those projections with actual results. AI is used to update rolling forecasts more frequently than monthly or quarterly cycles allow, pulling in transaction data, payroll, sales pipelines, and external indicators. In revenue models, external signals such as hiring trends, commodity prices, interest rates, and public filings can be ingested to adjust assumptions. Variance analysis and explanation uses AI to flag differences between plan and actual, then draft narrative explanations for controllers and finance teams. Capital spending decisions and zero-based budgeting are also being supported by models that rank projects, test scenarios, and challenge baseline costs. The aim is not to replace finance judgment but to shorten the cycle and widen the set of scenarios a team can review.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature, especially data aggregation, anomaly detection, and first draft variance commentary. Rolling forecasts can now be refreshed daily or weekly in many systems, though the quality depends on clean source data and clear ownership of assumptions. External signals in revenue models remain harder because correlation is not causation and many signals are noisy, delayed, or revised. Capital spending decisions still require strategic judgment about risk, timing, and competitive position, and models cannot settle those trade offs. Zero-based budgeting is often more of a process and culture change than a modeling problem, so AI helps with cost visibility but does not by itself create budget discipline. The honest limit is that AI can generate plausible explanations and scenarios, but finance teams must verify them against contracts, accounting rules, and business context.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section form a chain from continuous planning to specific decisions, and a reader can move from the general forecasting cycle into any one of them depending on whether the question is about cadence, inputs, explanation, investment, or cost base. Rolling Forecasts covers the mechanics of frequent updates and the data pipelines that feed them. External Signals in Revenue Models looks at how outside indicators, including the 355 merger and acquisition filings the site tracks, enter the revenue plan and where those inputs can mislead. Variance Analysis and Explanation deals with the comparison of plan to actual and the drafting of commentary for management. Capital Spending Decisions focuses on long lived investments, hurdle rates, and scenario testing for large commitments. Zero-Based Budgeting examines the practice of rebuilding costs from zero rather than adjusting last year's base.
